question: Total intravenous anaesthesia (TIVA) with propofol infusion is the preferred maintenance technique for patients at high risk of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) and those undergoing ear or airway surgery where volatile agents may be problematic.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Propofol-based TIVA reduces PONV risk (propofol has direct anti-emetic effects) and avoids the need to share the airway circuit with volatile agent delivery — particularly advantageous in ENT, airway surgery, and patients with high PONV risk scores.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Propofol has intrinsic anti-emetic properties and does not require shared airway delivery (unlike volatile agents), making TIVA ideal for PONV-prone patients and airway or ENT surgery where a gas-shared airway is undesirable.
